word_for_word: परेशः प्राप्यते शुद्धभक्त्येति स्थितमष्टमे। नवमे तु तदैश्वर्यमत्याश्चर्यं प्रपञ्च्यते।।1।।
In the eighth it was established that the Supreme Lord is attained by pure devotion; in the ninth His exceedingly wondrous lordship is elaborated.
एवं तावत्सप्तमाष्टमयोः स्वीयं पारमेश्वरं तत्त्वं भक्त्यैव सुलभं नान्यथेत्युक्त्वा
Thus, having said in the seventh and eighth chapters that His own supreme divine reality is easily attainable only through devotion and not otherwise,
इदानीमचिन्त्यं स्वकीयमैश्वर्यं भक्तेश्चासाधारणप्रभावं प्रपञ्चयिष्यन् श्रीभगवानुवाच -- इदंत्विति।
now, intending to elaborate His inconceivable lordship and the extraordinary power of devotion, the Blessed Lord says: ‘But this.’
विशेषेण ज्ञायतेऽनेनेति विज्ञानमुपासनं तत्सहितं ज्ञानमीश्वरविषयमिदं
‘Vijñāna’ is that by which something is known distinctly, namely worship or realization; this knowledge concerning the Lord is accompanied by it.
अनसूयवे ... ते तुभ्यं वक्ष्यामि।
I shall speak it to you, who are free from fault-finding toward Me, the supremely compassionate One, even though I repeatedly teach My own greatness.
तुशब्दो वैशिष्ट्ये।
The word ‘tu’ marks distinction.
तदेवाह -- गुह्यतममित्यादिना।
He states that distinction by ‘most secret’ and the rest.
गुह्यं धर्मज्ञानं ... ततोऽपि परमात्मज्ञानमतिरहस्यत्वाद्गुह्यतमम्।
Knowledge of dharma is secret; knowledge of the self distinct from the body and so forth is more secret; knowledge of the Supreme Self is most secret because it is exceedingly hidden.
यज्ज्ञात्वाऽशुभात्संसारान्मोक्ष्यसे सद्य एव मुक्तो भविष्यति।
Knowing this, you will be freed from the inauspicious saṃsāra; you will become liberated immediately.
किंच -- राजविद्येति।
Further: ‘the king of sciences.’
इदं ज्ञानं राजविद्या विद्यानां राजेति राजविद्या च।
This knowledge is the king of sciences, the sovereign among sciences.
गुह्यानां राजेति राजगुह्यं विद्यासु गोप्येषु च रहस्यम्। अतिश्रेष्ठमित्यर्थः।
It is the king among secrets, hence the royal secret, the supreme mystery among sciences and hidden things; the meaning is that it is exceedingly excellent.
राजदन्तादित्वादुपसर्जनस्य परत्वम्। राज्ञां विद्या राज्ञां गुह्यमितिवा
Because the compound belongs to the rājadanta class, the subordinate member comes later; or it may mean ‘the science of kings’ and ‘the secret of kings.’
उत्तमं पवित्रमत्यन्तपावनमिदं
It is supreme and purifying, utterly sanctifying.
ज्ञानिनां प्रत्यक्षावगमं च प्रत्यक्षः स्पष्टोऽवगमोऽवबोधो यस्य तत्प्रत्यक्षावगमम्। दृष्टफलमित्यर्थः।
For knowers it is directly apprehended: its apprehension and understanding are immediate and clear. The meaning is that its fruit is directly experienced.
धर्म्यं च धर्मादनपेतं सर्वधर्मफलत्वात्।
It is righteous, not departing from dharma, because it is the fruit of all dharmas.
कर्तुं सुसुखं च। सुखेन कर्तुं शक्यमित्यर्थः।
It is very easy to practice; that is, it can be done with ease.
अव्ययमक्षयफलत्वात्।
It is imperishable because its fruit is inexhaustible.
नन्वेवमस्यातिसुकरत्वे के नाम संसारिणः स्युस्तत्राह -- अश्रद्दधाना इति।
But if it is so very easy, who indeed would remain in saṃsāra? To this He says: ‘Those without faith.’
अस्य भक्तिलक्षणज्ञानसहितस्य धर्मस्येति कर्मणिषष्ठ्यौ।
The genitives in ‘of this dharma characterized by devotion and accompanied by knowledge’ are objective genitives.
इमं धर्ममश्रद्दधाना आस्तिक्येनास्वीकुर्वन्तः
Those who have no faith in this dharma, who do not accept it with the conviction that it is true,
उपायान्तरेण मत्प्राप्तये कृतप्रयत्ना अपि मामप्राप्य मृत्युयुक्ते संसारवर्त्मनि निवर्तन्ते।
even though striving to attain Me by another means, fail to attain Me and return to the path of saṃsāra joined with death.
मृत्युव्याप्ते संसारमार्गे परिभ्रमन्तीत्यर्थः।
The meaning is that they wander on the path of saṃsāra pervaded by death.
तदेवं वक्तव्यतया प्रस्तुतस्य ज्ञानस्य स्तुत्या श्रोतारमभिमुखीकृत्य तदेव ज्ञानं कथयति -- मयेति द्वाभ्याम्।
Thus, having made the hearer attentive by praising the knowledge introduced for explanation, He now states that very knowledge in two verses beginning ‘By Me.’
अव्यक्ता अतीन्द्रिया मूर्तिः स्वरूपं यस्य तादृशेन मया कारणभूतेन सर्वमिदं जगत्ततं व्याप्तम्
By Me, whose form or nature is unmanifest and beyond the senses, and who am the cause, this entire universe is pervaded.
तत्सृष्ट्वा तदेवानुप्राविशत् इति श्रुतेः।
For scripture says: ‘Having created it, He entered into it.’
अतएव कारणभूते मयि तिष्ठन्तीति मत्स्थानि सर्वाणि चराचराणि भूतानि।
Therefore all moving and unmoving beings abide in Me, their cause, and are said to be ‘situated in Me.’
एवमपि घटादिषु स्वकार्येषु मृत्तिकेव तेषु भूतेषु नाहमवस्थित आकाशवदसङ्गत्वात्।
Even so, I am not situated in those beings as clay is in its effects such as pots, because like space I am unattached.
किंच -- नचेति। नच मयि स्थितानि भूतान्यसङ्गत्वादेव मम।
Further: ‘And beings are not situated in Me,’ precisely because I am unattached.
ननु तर्हि व्यापकत्वमाश्रयत्वं च पूर्वोक्तं विरुद्धमित्याशङ्क्याह -- यथेति।
If so, the previously stated pervasion and being the support would seem contradictory; anticipating this, He says: ‘Behold.’
म ऐश्वरमसाधारणं योगं युक्तिमघटितघटनाचातुर्यं पश्य।
Behold My unique divine yoga, the skill of making the apparently impossible possible.
मदीययोगमायावैभवस्यावितर्क्यत्वान्न विरुद्धं किंचिदित्यर्थः।
Because the majesty of My yogamāyā is beyond reasoning, there is no contradiction; this is the meaning.
अन्यदप्याश्चर्यं पश्येत्याह -- भूतेति।
He says ‘supporting beings’ to show another wonder.
भूतानि बिभर्ति धारयतीति भूतभृत्। भूतानि भावयति पालयतीति भूतभावनः।
‘Bhūtabhṛt’ means He who bears and supports beings; ‘bhūtabhāvana’ means He who causes beings to flourish and protects them.
एवंभूतोऽपि ममात्मा परं स्वरूपं भूतस्थो न भवति।
Even though such, My Self, My supreme nature, is not situated in beings.
अयंभावः ... निरहंकारत्वादिति।

The purport is: just as the individual self, while bearing and protecting the body, remains joined to it through egoism, I, though supporting and protecting beings, do not abide in them because I am free from egoism.
असंश्लिष्टयोरप्याधाराधेयभावं दृष्टान्तेनाह -- यथेति।
He illustrates how the relation of support and supported can exist even without contact: ‘As.’
अवकाशं विनाऽवस्थानानुपपत्तेर्नित्यमाकाशस्थितो वायुः सर्वत्रगोऽपि महानपि नाकाशेन संश्लिष्यते निरवयवत्वेन संश्लेषायोगात्
Because nothing can remain without space, the wind always abides in space; though vast and moving everywhere it is not joined to space, since space is partless and contact with it is impossible.
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मयि स्थितानीति जानीहि।
In the same way, know that all beings are situated in Me.
तदेवमसङ्गस्य योगमायया स्थितिहेतुत्वमुक्तम्
Thus it has been said that although unattached, He is the cause of beings’ continuance through yogamāyā.
तयैव सृष्टिप्रलयहेतुत्वं चाह -- सर्वेति।
He now says that through that same power He is the cause of creation and dissolution: ‘All.’
कल्पक्षये प्रलयकाले सर्वाणि भूतानि मदीयां प्रकृतिं यान्ति त्रिगुणात्मिकायां मायायां लीयन्ते
At the end of a kalpa, at the time of dissolution, all beings enter My prakṛti, dissolving into māyā composed of the three guṇas.
पुनः कल्पादौ सृष्टिकाले तानि विसृजामि विशेषेण सृजामि।
Again, at the beginning of a kalpa, at creation, I send them forth, creating them distinctly.
नन्वसङ्गो निर्विकारश्च त्वं कथं सृजसीत्यपेक्षायामाह -- प्रकृतिमिति द्वाभ्याम्।
But how do You, being unattached and changeless, create? In response He says in two verses beginning ‘Prakṛti.’
स्वां स्वाधीनां प्रकृतिमवष्टभ्याधिष्ठाय
Having taken hold of and presided over My own prakṛti, which is under My control,
प्रलये लीनं सन्तं चतुर्विधमिमं सर्वं भूतग्रामं कर्मादिपरवशं पुनःपुनर्विविधं सृजामि विशेषेण सृजामीति वा।
I repeatedly create in diverse forms this entire fourfold multitude of beings that had dissolved at pralaya and is dependent on karma and the like; or, I create it distinctly.
कथम्। प्रकृतेर्वशात्प्राचीनकर्मनिमित्ततत्स्वभावबलात्।
How? Under the force of prakṛti, that is, by the power of their nature conditioned by previous karma.
ननु एवं नानाविधानि कर्माणि कुर्वतस्तव जीववद्वन्धः कथं न स्यादित्याशङ्क्याह -- नचेति।
If You perform many kinds of actions in this way, why are You not bound like an individual soul? Anticipating this, He says: ‘And those actions.’
तानि सृष्ट्यादीनि कर्माणि मां न निबध्न्ति।
Those actions such as creation do not bind Me.
कर्मासक्तिर्हि बन्धहेतुः सा चाप्तकामत्वान्मम नास्ति
Attachment to action is the cause of bondage, and because all My desires are fulfilled, I have no such attachment.
अत उदासीनवद्वर्तमानस्य मे बन्धनं नापादयन्ति।
Therefore they do not produce bondage for Me, who remain like one indifferent.
उदासीनत्वे कर्तृत्वानुपपत्तेरुदासीनवत्स्थितमित्युक्तम्।
Since actual indifference would be incompatible with agency, the text says ‘situated like one indifferent.’
तदेवोपपादयति -- मयेति।
He establishes that very point: ‘Under My supervision.’
मयाध्यक्षेणाधिष्ठात्रा निमित्तभूतेन प्रकृतिः सचराचरं विश्वं सूयते जनयति।
Prakṛti, under Me as superintendent and presiding efficient cause, gives birth to the universe with its moving and unmoving beings.
अनेन मदधिष्ठानेन हेतुना इदं जगद्विपरिवर्तते पुनःपुनर्जायते।
Because of this presiding presence of Mine, the world revolves and is born again and again.
संनिधिमात्रेणाधिष्ठातृत्वात्कर्तृत्वमुदासीनत्वं चाविरुद्धमिति भावः।
Because His superintendence is through mere presence, agency and being like one indifferent are not contradictory; this is the purport.
नन्वेवंभूतं परमेश्वरं त्वां किमिति केचिन्नाद्रियन्ते तत्राह -- अवजानन्तीति द्वाभ्याम्।
Why do some not honor You, the Supreme Lord of such a nature? To this He answers in two verses beginning ‘They disregard Me.’
सर्वभूतमहेश्वररूपं मदीयं परं भावं तत्त्वमजानन्तो मूढा मूर्खा मामवजानन्त्यवमन्यन्ते।
Fools, not knowing My supreme nature and reality as the great Lord of all beings, disregard and despise Me.
अवज्ञाने हेतुः शुद्धसत्वमयीमपि तनुं भक्तेच्छावशान्मनुष्याकारामाश्रितवन्तम्।
The cause of their disregard is that, though My body consists of pure sattva, I have assumed a human form in accordance with the desire of devotees.
किंच -- मोघाशा इति।
Further: ‘vain hopes.’
मत्तोऽन्यद्देवतान्तरं क्षिप्रं फलं दास्यतीत्येवंभूता मोघा निष्फलैवाशा येषां ते।
Their hope that some deity other than Me will quickly give the desired fruit is vain and fruitless.
अतएव मद्विमुखत्वान्मोघानि व्यर्थानि कर्माणि येषां ते।
Therefore, because they turn away from Me, their actions are vain and useless.
मोघमेव नानाकुतर्काश्रितं शास्त्रज्ञानं येषां ते।
Their scriptural knowledge too is vain, resting on various false reasonings.
अतएव विचेतसो विक्षिप्तचित्ताः।
Therefore they are senseless, their minds distracted.
सर्वत्र हेतुः। राक्षसीं तामसीं हिंसादिप्रचुराम् आसुरीं च राजसीं कामदर्पादिबहुलाम् मोहिनीं बुद्धिभ्रंशकरीं प्रकृतिं स्वभावं श्रिताः ...

The cause in every case is that they have resorted to a deluding nature: rākṣasī, tamasic and abounding in violence and the like, or āsurī, rajasic and abounding in desire, pride and the like, which destroys right understanding; thus the construction continues from the previous verse: they disregard Me.
के तर्हि त्वामाराधयन्तीत्यत आह -- महात्मानस्त्विति।
Who, then, worship You? He says: ‘But the great souls.’
महात्मानः कामाद्यनभिभूतचित्ताः
Great souls are those whose minds are not overpowered by desire and the rest,
यतोऽभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिरित्यादिना वक्ष्यमाणां दैवीं प्रकृतिं स्वभावमाश्रिताः।
because they have taken refuge in the divine nature that will be described by ‘fearlessness, purity of mind’ and so on.
अतएव मद्व्यतिरेकेण नास्त्यन्यस्मिन्मनो येषां ते
Therefore their mind is nowhere apart from Me; they are single-minded.
भूतादिं जगत्कारणमव्ययं नित्यं च मां ज्ञात्वा भजन्ति।
Knowing Me as the origin of beings, the cause of the universe, imperishable and eternal, they worship Me.
तेषां भजनप्रकारमाह -- सततमिति द्वाभ्याम्।
He describes how they worship in two verses beginning ‘Always.’
सततं सर्वदा स्तोत्रमन्त्रादिभिः कीर्तयन्तः केचिन्मामुपासते सेवन्ते
Some worship and serve Me by always praising Me with hymns, mantras and the like.
दृढानि व्रतानि नियमा येषां तादृशाः सन्तो यतन्तश्चेश्वरपूजादिषु इन्द्रियोपसंहारादिषु प्रयत्नं कुर्वन्तश्च
With firm vows and observances, they strive in worship of the Lord and in restraining the senses and the like.
केचिद्भक्त्या नमस्यन्तः प्रणमन्तश्चान्ये नित्ययुक्ता अनवरतमवहिताः सर्वे सेवन्ते भक्त्येति नित्ययुक्ता इति च कीर्तनादिष्वपि द्रष्टव्यम्।

Others bow down with devotion; all are constantly united and uninterruptedly attentive in their service. ‘With devotion’ and ‘constantly united’ are to be understood as applying also to praising and the other practices.
किंच -- ज्ञानेति।
Further: ‘by the sacrifice of knowledge.’
वासुदेवः सर्वमित्येवं सर्वात्मत्वदर्शनं ज्ञानं तदेव यज्ञस्तेन ज्ञानयज्ञेन मां यजन्तः पूजयन्तोऽन्येऽप्युपासते
Others worship Me by the sacrifice of knowledge: the knowledge that sees Vāsudeva as everything and as the Self of all is itself the sacrifice; by that they sacrifice to and worship Me.
तत्रापि केचिदेकत्वेन एकमेव परं ब्रह्मेति परमार्थदर्शनरूपाभेदभावनया
Among them some worship with the conception of unity, the non-difference arising from the highest vision that there is one Supreme Brahman alone.
केचित्पृथक्त्वेन दासोऽहमिति पृथग्भावनया
Some worship with a conception of distinction, thinking ‘I am His servant.’
केचित्तु विश्वतोमुखं सर्वात्मकं मां बहुधा ब्रह्मरुद्रादिरूपेणोपासते।
Others worship Me, whose faces are everywhere and who am the Self of all, in many forms such as Brahmā and Rudra.
सर्वात्मतां प्रपञ्चयति -- अहमिति चतुर्भिः।
He elaborates His being the Self of all in four verses beginning ‘I am.’
क्रतुः श्रौतोऽग्निष्टोमादिः
‘Kratu’ is a Vedic sacrifice such as Agniṣṭoma.
यज्ञस्तु स्मार्तः पञ्चयज्ञादिः
‘Yajña’ is a Smārta rite such as the five great sacrifices.
स्वधा पित्रर्थे श्राद्धादिः
‘Svadhā’ is a rite such as śrāddha performed for the ancestors.
औषधमोषधिप्रभवमन्नं भेषजं वा
‘Auṣadha’ is food produced from herbs, or medicine.
मन्त्रो याज्यापुरोनुवाक्यादिः
‘Mantra’ means formulas such as yājyā and puronuvākyā.
आज्यं होमादिसाधनम्
‘Ājya’ is clarified butter and other means of oblation.
अग्निराहवनीयादिः
‘Fire’ means the Āhavanīya and the other sacred fires.
हुतं होमः
‘Offering’ means the act of oblation.
एतत्सर्वमहमेव।
All of this is I alone.
Further: ‘the father.’
धाता कर्मफलविधाता
‘Dhātā’ is the ordainer of the fruits of karma.
वेद्यं ज्ञेयं वस्तु
‘That which is to be known’ is the object of knowledge.
पवित्रं शोधकं प्रायश्चित्तात्मकं वा
‘Purifier’ means that which purifies, or an expiatory rite.
ओंकारः प्रणवः
‘Oṃkāra’ is the praṇava.
ऋग्वेदादयो वेदाश्च अहमेव
The Vedas such as Ṛg are also I alone.
स्पष्टमन्यत्।
The rest is clear.
